title: The asymmetric heartbeat: heart-rate asymmetry (a newly-authored op), bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2

dataset.name: Fantasia Database
dataset.record: subject f1y01 (young), first 5-min RR window (391 intervals); cohort-consistency uses all 10 subjects
dataset.citation: Iyengar N, Peng CK, Morin R, Goldberger AL, Lipsitz LA. Age-related alterations in the fractal scaling of cardiac interbeat interval dynamics. Am J Physiol 1996;271(4):R1078-R1084. Fantasia Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The Poincare plot is NOT symmetric: heart-rate decelerations (RR prolongations, points above the line of identity) and accelerations (shortenings, below) contribute unequally to variability -- heart-rate asymmetry (HRA), a signature of the temporal irreversibility of cardiac dynamics that the symmetric SD1/SD2 cannot capture. The ecosystem had only SD1/SD2; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, ecgHRVasymmetry, that computes the HRA descriptors (Guzik/Slope/Area/Porta indices + the deceleration/acceleration contributions). On a real 5-minute RR window it reproduces NeuroKit2's hrv_nonlinear HRA indices BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~1e-14), and it recovers the HRA signature: decelerations contribute more than accelerations to short-term variability (C1d 0.63 > C1a 0.37), robust across the cohort (8/10 subjects).

claims.statement: Guzik's Index (%) -- deceleration-point distance contribution (>50 indicates deceleration asymmetry)
Porta's Index (%) -- fraction of points below the line of identity (accelerations)
contribution of DECELERATIONS to short-term HRV (C1d) -- the larger short-term component
contribution of ACCELERATIONS to short-term HRV (C1a) -- the smaller short-term component
contribution of decelerations to long-term HRV (C2d) -- the smaller long-term component
contribution of accelerations to long-term HRV (C2a) -- the larger long-term component
max |ecgHRVasymmetry - NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear| over all HRA indices (bit-exact)
subjects (of 10) where C1d > C1a -- decelerations dominate short-term variability (HRA signature robustness)

validation.reference: The newly-authored ecgHRVasymmetry op is validated against NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear, an established HRV toolbox. NeuroKit2 re-computes the HRA indices (GI/SI/AI/PI + the deceleration/acceleration contributions C1d/C1a/C2d/C2a) from the same RR (peaks reconstructed from the integer-ms RR at 250 Hz so NeuroKit2 sees the identical series). The agreement is BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~1e-14 over all indices) because the op implements the identical Piskorski-Guzik formulas. The finding: C1d 0.63 > C1a 0.37 (decelerations dominate short-term variability), robust across the Fantasia cohort (8/10 subjects); C2a 0.64 > C2d 0.36 (accelerations dominate long-term) on this subject.
validation.data: REAL -- Fantasia (PhysioNet), subject f1y01 5-min RR for the certified op; all 10 subjects for the cohort-consistency count
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored ecgHRVasymmetry reproduces NeuroKit2 hrv_nonlinear's HRA indices bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~1e-14); (2) decelerations dominate short-term variability (C1d 0.63 > C1a 0.37), robust in 8/10 subjects. HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to fill a genuine gap -- the ecosystem had only the symmetric SD1/SD2 (ecgHRVpoincare); ecgHRVasymmetry adds the GI/SI/AI/PI indices + the C1d/C1a/C2d/C2a/Cd/Ca contributions; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op implements the IDENTICAL Piskorski-Guzik / NeuroKit2 formulas, so the ~1e-14 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) the finding -- C1d > C1a, decelerations dominate short-term variability -- is the established HRA signature (a vagal / temporal-irreversibility marker), robust across the cohort (8/10); the complementary long-term asymmetry (C2a > C2d) holds on this subject but is weaker/mixed across the small cohort (5/10), and NO age direction is claimed (n=5+5, and HRA age effects are cohort-dependent); (4) a descriptive read on a 5-min window of one subject for the certified op; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic closed form).

open_questions.q: HRA is prognostic: reduced deceleration-driven short-term asymmetry has been associated with increased mortality after myocardial infarction (the deceleration-capacity literature). Computing the effective HRA over a clinical cohort with outcomes -- and pairing it with the DFA alpha1 and Poincare SD1/SD2 on the same beats -- would test whether the asymmetry adds prognostic information beyond the symmetric descriptors. Documented, not escalated.
